checks: Nondecreasing adjacent slopes are equivalent to all supporting-slope inequalities by telescoping and one-sided endpoint choices. A large constant is feasible and nonnegative objective sublevels are compact, including a singleton interval.

Polyhedral normal-cone stationarity gives λ=s+2β−β_left−β_right. Positive β forces adjacent slopes equal, so equal opposite convexity flows use only tight original inequalities and satisfy the original slope equations.

For q>1, complementarity prevents flow leaving the zero-height set, and summing stationarity rules out incoming flow and its λ. Conservation and row mean then annihilate all internal nonzero-displacement flow by the squared-distance identity.

Uniform positive stopping probability on the retained finite set gives the convergent resolvent. The equation a=λ+aT and aD=s identify the original coupling's terminal masses. Multiplying D+T−Id by N gives the exact second-difference row identity and testing linear f gives mean i.

Reachability in the positive β component gives positivity exactly there. N=Id+NT yields the stated tridiagonal equation, and each adjacent stopping site's mass is the neighboring Green weight. Complementarity gives the affine height interval.

Strict residual projection is an interval, and compact residual midpoint comparison rules out positive second differences at sites with both neighbors nonempty. Three empty residuals contribute zero. Thus only boundaries and adjacent exterior sites can carry positive terms.
The frozen source links separately cover the KKT realization, Green identity, and boundary loss localization. The source's separate conditional critical-cap application is not a premise.

The six-triangle witness has one explicit nearest-neighbor component and a concrete Green row; it is a single-case calculation and does not imply the general KKT and boundary result.
